# @bangbang93/opencode-write-existing-file-guard

An [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) plugin that stops a session from overwriting a file it has not read.

`write` replaces a whole file, so one wrong guess about its content is enough to wipe it. The plugin lets a session
overwrite an existing file only after the session read it with the `read` tool. A blocked call fails with
`File already exists: <path>. Read it with the read tool before you overwrite it.`

## Install

Add the package to `plugins` in `opencode.jsonc`:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": ["@bangbang93/opencode-write-existing-file-guard@0.1.0"]
}
```

To run a checkout of the repository instead, point the entry at `packages/write-existing-file-guard`.

## Behavior

- `write` to a file that does not exist yet is always allowed.
- `write` to an existing file is allowed once for every `read` of that file in the same session, and blocked
  otherwise.
- A read counts when it completed. A denied or failed read grants nothing.
- When a session overwrites a file, what other sessions have read of it stops counting, because their copy is
  outdated.
- A file is tracked by its real path, so a symlink or a `..` segment leads to the same entry.
- Only files inside the project directory are guarded.

## Limits

- `edit` and `patch` are not guarded, and neither are shell commands that write a file.
- Sessions are independent, and a subagent has its own session. It has to read a file itself before it overwrites it,
  even when the session that started it has read the file.
- The record of reads lives in memory. After OpenCode restarts, or when an old session is resumed, the session has
  to read the file again.
- At most 256 sessions and 1024 files per session are remembered, the least recently used first to go.

## Disable

Add `"-write-existing-file-guard"` to the `plugins` array.

## License

MIT. [NOTICE.md](./NOTICE.md) lists what this plugin derives from.

# Notice

This plugin re-implements the write-existing-file-guard hook of
[oh-my-openagent](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent) 5.1.24 for the OpenCode V2 plugin API.

## Sources

- Hook design: `packages/omo-opencode/src/hooks/write-existing-file-guard/` of oh-my-openagent 5.1.24, commit
  `fda8eb83630682c22a18e06b51b7366f843858b9` (Sustainable Use License v1.0). No source text from that package is
  included here.

## Differences from the oh-my-openagent hook

- A read is registered in `ctx.tool.hook("execute.after")` once it completed. The original registered it before the
  read ran, so a read that was denied or failed also allowed the overwrite.
- There is no `overwrite` argument and no exemption for `.omo/**`. OpenCode 2.4's `write` tool has no such argument,
  and `.omo` is the workspace of oh-my-openagent's own planning tools.
- The error names the file and says to read it first.
- Records are dropped when the caps are reached. The plugin does not listen for `session.deleted`.

## Dependencies

- `@opencode/plugin` must stay compatible with the OpenCode release that loads the plugin.

## Disable

Add `"-write-existing-file-guard"` to the `plugins` array in `opencode.jsonc`.
